question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` allow scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what grammar and scheme limits are acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: This changes which browser origins may reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and current docs intentionally describe full-origin allowlisting plus the global `*` as the only wildcard policy.

options.title: Approve constrained extension wildcard grammar
options.body: Define a small explicit grammar for extension-scheme wildcards, implement it in the shared helper, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Fold into broader origin-pattern contract
options.body: Wait for the loopback pattern work to settle and decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in the same public config contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained extension wildcard grammar
recommendation.body: Define a small explicit grammar for extension-scheme wildcards, implement it in the shared helper, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the Gateway origin boundary and merged the existing wildcard allowlist behavior, so this security policy decision is closest to his feature history.
